target.title: feat(whatsapp): add requester-bound MeowCaller calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp-connected agents cannot place a WhatsApp voice call back to the person who triggered a turn. This adds an experimental, requester-bound call tool for audible task-completion or urgent notifications.

Closes #99634

## Why This Change Was Made

The WhatsApp plugin registers `whatsapp_call` only for WhatsApp-originated turns carrying trusted requester context and only when `channels.whatsapp.actions.calls` is explicitly `true`. The tool accepts a message but no destination, resolves the requester from inbound identity, synthesizes telephony TTS, and invokes a separately paired MeowCaller companion with fixed `notify` arguments.

The companion contract is explicit and send-only: the reviewed [MeowCaller PR #7](https://github.com/purpshell/meowcaller/pull/7) adds `pair` and `notify`, and `notify` exits successfully only after answer, playback, and hangup. OpenClaw pins the reviewed MeowCaller commit in its setup documentation and keeps the companion's linked-device credentials separate from the normal WhatsApp channel session.

## User Impact

Calls are experimental and disabled by default. After setting `channels.whatsapp.actions.calls` to `true` in `openclaw.json`, installing the pinned MeowCaller CLI, pairing its separate linked-device session, and configuring TTS, a user can message: `Call me and say the build finished.`

Boundaries:

- calls only the current WhatsApp requester; there is no destination argument
- omits the tool unless calls are explicitly enabled
- rejects self-calls and concurrent calls for one account
- supports PCM and mu-law telephony TTS outputs
- limits synthesized audio to 60 seconds
- deletes private temporary audio after each attempt
- uses explicit store, answer-timeout, and max-duration arguments
- reports success only when MeowCaller exits with code 0 after playback and hangup
- emits POSIX or PowerShell pairing instructions for the current platform
- budgets the full companion lifecycle: 60-second connect wait, 45-second answer timeout, audio playback, and shutdown grace (115-175 seconds total)

No new environment variables.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/agent-tools-call.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-schema.test.ts src/config/zod-schema.providers-whatsapp.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/index.test.ts` — 35/35 passed
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwp4299mpkbc9mbgkthvnead` — WhatsApp extension suite passed: 86 files and 999/999 tests
- Same Testbox — scoped formatting, generated bundled-channel metadata, WhatsApp MDX, and 5,547-link audit passed
- [Testbox Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28700611995)
- MeowCaller: `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go build -o /tmp/meowcaller-notify ./cmd/meowcaller` passed
- Fresh Codex autoreview found no actionable defects and rated the default-off config delta correct at 0.98 confidence
- Upstream implementation: [purpshell/meowcaller#7](https://github.com/purpshell/meowcaller/pull/7)

Known proof gap: no end-to-end call was placed because the interactive MeowCaller QR session was not paired. The capability is therefore documented as experimental, remains disabled by default, and requires an operator-controlled companion pairing before it can be exposed.
